(= ARQ-058, ADR-0004) Split representation, resolved by user decision this session: existing runtime code (packages/geometry-2d's coordinate-system.ts, packages/editor-shell's viewport-controller.ts and every snap-*.ts, metric/imperial numeric-input parsers) keeps double-precision floating-point millimetres unchanged - zero migration of shipped, tested code, and it matches IFC/DXF's own native floating-point representation with no lossy import/export conversion. The canonical .arq storage and cross-platform semantic hash (ARQ-200, ARQ-214, ARQ-222, ARQ-224) instead use exact integer micrometres (i64), because docs/architecture/SHARED-RUST-CORE.md requires 'the same model operation must produce the same semantic result and model hash on all supported targets' and explicitly forbids 'platform-dependent floating-point formatting as a canonical value' - raw floats risk drift between native Rust, WASM and JS. Documented edge: Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER (2^53) micrometres is approximately 9,000 km, far beyond any building-scale project - a noted boundary, not a real limit.
Native SQLite `.arq` file format: application ID 0x41525131 ("ARQ1"), versioned schema via PRAGMA user_version, frozen v1 header (see docs/architecture/ARQ-FILE-FORMAT.md)

Shared Rust core for deterministic operations, validation, hashing and migrations, plus selected geometry predicates only - compiled to native and WebAssembly targets. Narrowly scoped: does not replace TypeScript UI or renderer code, and does not (yet) implement the full module list in docs/architecture/SHARED-RUST-CORE.md speculatively ahead of real need.
Local-first replica: every device edits a local project replica; sync moves typed operations and content-addressed resources only, never raw SQLite pages
Canonical (.arq) and derived (device-local, replaceable, reproducible) data are strictly separated - see D-007's narrowed scope
Progressive project opening: open the last active view from indexed canonical data before loading inactive resources and 3D detail

SQLite WebAssembly loaded directly in an Arq-owned dedicated Worker (not the deprecated Worker1/Promiser APIs); opfs-sahpool as the primary single-writer VFS, opfs/opfs-wl benchmarked for multi-tab; one active project writer enforced via application lock + BroadcastChannel

Three.js WebGLRenderer as the Release 1 production 3D renderer; WebGPURenderer kept as a separate benchmarked capability/lab branch, not a Release 1 dependency, promoted only after visual/device/performance/context-loss parity passes

React Aria Components as the primary foundation for ordinary interface controls, with a controlled escape to lower-level hooks for specialist widgets; custom canvas interactions must provide equivalent keyboard/focus/status/assistive-technology access through the model tree, inspector and command system

.arq has two valid physical containers for one unchanged logical content (@arq/project-format's manifest/model/operations/views/sheets, ARQ-076 through ARQ-080, with its own existing migration registry): the new SQLite file (ADR-0019, D-015) is the live working project file; the existing zip-of-files archive remains the portable export/interchange format. packages/arqfs (ARQ-195) stores @arq/project-format's existing entries as SQLite rows/blobs rather than reimplementing serialization, checksums or migration.
